title: `toc_tokens` names contain internal placeholder junk for headers with raw HTML or entities
spec: This is the Python-Markdown library (Python 3, no dependencies). Run the tests with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -q`. When a header contains raw HTML or an HTML entity, the `name` in `md.toc_tokens` contains internal placeholder strings instead of text. ``` md = markdown.Markdown(extensions=['markdown.extensions.toc']) md.convert('# Foo Bar Baz.') md.toc_tokens ``` Expected: ``` [{'level': 1, 'id': 'foo-bar-baz', 'name': 'Foo Bar Baz.', 'children': []}] ``` Actual: ``` [{'level': 1, 'id': 'foo-bar-baz', 'name': 'Foo \x02wzxhzdk:0\x03Bar\x02wzxhzdk:1\x03 Baz.', 'children': []}] ``` Likewise `# Foo & bar` gives the name `'Foo \x02wzxhzdk:0\x03 bar'`; expected `'Foo & bar'` (the entity is kept, as in the HTML). A label set with `attr_list` (`# Header 4 { data-toc-label="Foo Baz" }`) has the same problem. The TOC is meant to hold plain text: tags are stripped and entities kept. That should hold for both `md.toc` and `md.toc_tokens`. Note `md.toc` currently keeps raw tags for such headers (`Foo Bar Baz.`); it should show `Foo Bar Baz.` too, and a `data-toc-label` of `Foo Baz` should appear as `Foo Baz` in both.
acceptance: Headers with raw HTML give plain-text names in `toc_tokens` and `toc`, with no placeholder characters
Entities in headers are kept (e.g. `Foo & bar`) in both outputs, and `data-toc-label` values are handled the same way
